text: In 1930s Prague, Karel Kopfrkingl tends his beloved crematorium, his "Temple of Death", reading Tibetan mysticism and believing [the ovens liberate the souls he burns|images|graves, coffins and funerals]. He is a fussy, abstinent family man, until an old army friend [presses a Nazi party flyer on him|trigger|saying yes to an offer] and assures him of a drop of German blood. As the Protectorate takes hold, his gentle devotion curdles toward [the wife and children he claims to love|wrong|killing within the family] and toward [the ovens of the camps|threat|the powerful and their systems].
